meta.storyTitle: Define memory entries and shared failures

summary.prose: This story creates the definitions every module shares: memory entries and their tagged names, source references, projects, session checkpoints and one failure type, with their checks written once. A definition checks itself when created, and retiring an entry, which records the time, is the only change it allows. The import test learns nested packages and rejects cycles between modules.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: agent_pfc/core holds only subpackages. core/common holds the shared definitions and core/utils the shared functions, each divided into modules by subject. locations, config, activity, identity, client and cache/embedding each do one job. An import table enforced by test keeps dependencies pointing one way.

ownedContracts.purpose: One definition of entries and their named entities, sources, projects, session checkpoints and the failures modules raise.

ownedContracts.interfaceSketch:
// Module core.utils.validation. Each check returns the accepted value or raises an invalid_input Failure naming the field.
interface Validation { requireText(field: string, value: unknown): string; requirePosition(field: string, value: unknown): number; requireOffsetTime(field: string, value: unknown): string }

boundary.internal: How entries and named entities are checked and represented in Python, the entries, checkpoints and failures modules of core/common, the validation module of core/utils, and the changes to the import-direction test for nested packages and module cycles.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Per-platform location rules, the configuration file format and its validation, including the compaction defaults, and how activity is written and rotated. Session archiving itself belongs to a later module.
The rule that identifies a project from a location and how it behaves across worktrees and machines.
Wire encoding, endpoint layout, version compatibility rule, time limits, the HTTP library and how failures are mapped to shared kinds.

The move of the embedding protocol into core/common, of its checks into core/utils and of its cache into core/cache/embedding, and the exact method signatures of the interfaces. The local model's instructions belong to the parser design and the calling agent's steering to the MCP adapter design. The loose matching technique, the ranking, the meaning of a score, how history is laid out and how compaction works are left to the store design, and starting compaction on schedule to the memory server design.

nonFunctional.observability: Every process records activity in the shape of sc5; the client records its calls through the activity package.
nonFunctional.durability: Updates are idempotent: the session checkpoint decides whether a change is applied, unchanged or out of sequence, and a checkpoint advances only with stored entries. The store design must keep this true across a failure between writing entries and advancing the checkpoint.

api.name: FailureKind
api.signature: class FailureKind(StrEnum): INVALID_INPUT, INVALID_CONFIGURATION, UNKNOWN_PROJECT, SERVER_UNREACHABLE, INCOMPATIBLE_VERSION, REQUEST_FAILED, BACKEND_FAILED  # values are the lower-case names

returns.meaning: One of the seven failure kinds.

postconditions: Each value equals the string in the approved contract.

api.name: Failure
api.signature: class Failure(Exception): __init__(self, kind: FailureKind, message: str); kind: FailureKind; message: str

parameters.name: kind
parameters.purpose: Lets a caller tell failures apart.

parameters.name: message
parameters.purpose: What went wrong, in words a user can act on.

returns.meaning: The one exception modules raise for shared failures.

errors.condition: kind is not a FailureKind; a programming error.
message is blank; a programming error.

api.name: Validation
api.signature: require_text(field: str, value: object) -> str; require_position(field: str, value: object) -> int; require_offset_time(field: str, value: object) -> str

parameters.name: field
parameters.purpose: Name used in the failure message.

errors.condition: require_text: not a string, or blank. require_position: not an integer, a boolean, or negative. require_offset_time: not an ISO 8601 string with a UTC offset.

postconditions: No value is trimmed or converted.

returns.meaning: Whether an entry is an instruction or a data point.
Whether an entry is in force.

parameters.name: value
parameters.purpose: Identifier of the project; how it is derived belongs to s3.

returns.meaning: A project identity usable as a dictionary key.

api.name: Source
api.signature: @dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True) class Source: agent: str; session_id: str; file: str; position: int; spoken_at: str

parameters.name: position
parameters.purpose: Where the message is in the file; its unit is set by the history reader.

parameters.name: spoken_at
parameters.purpose: When the message was written, as ISO 8601 with a UTC offset.

returns.meaning: A reference to the message an entry came from, without its wording.

errors.condition: A string fails require_text, position fails require_position or spoken_at fails require_offset_time.

api.name: Provenance
api.signature: @dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True) class Provenance: extraction_model: str; embedding_model: str

returns.meaning: The models that produced an entry.

api.name: NamedEntity
api.signature: @dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True) class NamedEntity: text: str; start: int; end: int

parameters.name: start
parameters.purpose: Index of the first character, counted in Python string positions.

returns.meaning: A tagged official name within an entry's text.

errors.condition: text is blank, a position is invalid, or end minus start differs from the length of text.

api.name: Entry
api.signature: @dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True) class Entry: id: str; project: ProjectId; kind: EntryKind; text: str; entities: tuple[NamedEntity, ...]; sources: tuple[Source, ...]; provenance: Provenance; status: EntryStatus; retired_at: str | None = None; replaced_by: str | None = None; retire(self, retired_at: str, replaced_by: str | None = None) -> None  # compares by value, not hashable

parameters.name: text
parameters.purpose: Normalized rule or fact, at most 500 characters counted as Python string positions.

parameters.name: sources
parameters.purpose: Where the entry came from; at least one.

parameters.name: retired_at
parameters.purpose: When the entry was retired, as ISO 8601 with a UTC offset. Required when retired and absent when active; the argument of retire is required.

parameters.name: replaced_by
parameters.purpose: Identifier of the entry that replaced a retired one.

returns.meaning: A checked entry that only retire can change.

errors.condition: On creation: kind or project is empty; a value has the wrong type; id or text is blank; text is longer than 500 characters; entities or sources is not a tuple of the right type; sources is empty; an entity differs from the text at its positions; a retired entry has no retired_at or one that fails require_offset_time; an active entry has retired_at or replaced_by; replaced_by is blank or equals id. The message names the field.
On retire: the entry is already retired, retired_at fails require_offset_time, or replaced_by is blank or equals id. Nothing changes.
A required argument is left out; a programming error.

postconditions: After retire, the same object has status retired, the given retirement time and the given replacement, and every other field is unchanged.
A retired entry may be created directly, with its retirement time and with or without a replacement, so that stored entries can be read back.
The definitions do not prevent an active copy of a retired entry; the store refuses it.

api.name: Checkpoint
api.signature: @dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True) class Checkpoint: agent: str; session_id: str; file: str; position: int; last_message_id: str; last_message_at: str

parameters.name: position
parameters.purpose: Where to proceed from in the file.

returns.meaning: How far one session has been processed.

errors.condition: A string fails require_text, position fails require_position or last_message_at fails require_offset_time.

postconditions: No comparison or update rule is defined here; that belongs to the store and server.

api.name: ImportTable
api.signature: ALLOWED: dict[str, frozenset[str]]  # dotted package path below agent_pfc -> packages or modules it may import; NAMESPACES: frozenset[str] = {'core', 'core.cache'}

returns.meaning: Violations; empty when every import follows the table and no modules form a cycle.

preconditions: Imports are read statically; dynamic importing stays forbidden.
postconditions: A module belongs to the longest table key that prefixes its path.
A module with no owning key is a violation unless it is the __init__ of a namespace.
A namespace __init__ holds only a docstring.
Every key starting 'core.' may import only keys starting 'core.'.
A cycle among project module imports is a violation naming the modules.

dataModelChanges.details: Module holding FailureKind and Failure. Imports nothing from the project, so the checks can import it without a cycle.
Module holding the three checks. Imports only the failures module.

Module holding EntryKind, EntryStatus, ProjectId, Source, Provenance, NamedEntity and Entry, with the 500-character limit. Imports the failures and validation modules. An entry owns its entities and sources.
Module holding Checkpoint. Imports the validation module.
Each __init__ holds only a docstring, so importing one module loads no other.
Keyed by dotted package paths, lists the approved core packages plus the existing embeddings package, which keeps its empty entry until s5 moves it, and gains the cycle check.
Replaced with the current project description, since it describes the removed design.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: The three common modules define every type in the contract with snake_case field names and tuples for lists. The existing EmbeddingBackendError is not touched; s5 moves it onto the backend_failed kind.
The validation module defines the three checks, and the definitions of this story use them.
The import test holds the approved table and namespaces, checks nested packages and rejects module cycles. Packages of later stories are listed now and created by those stories.

errorCases.scenario: An entry is created with an empty kind or project.
errorCases.detection: The entry's creation check tests both fields for no value before any other check.
errorCases.response: Failure with invalid_input naming the field.
errorCases.userImpact: The caller learns which value is missing; nothing is created.

errorCases.scenario: A value has the wrong type, such as a string for kind, a list for sources or a boolean for a position.
errorCases.detection: The shared checks and the creation checks test each field's type, treating a boolean as not an integer.
errorCases.response: Failure with invalid_input naming the field.
errorCases.userImpact: The caller learns which value is wrong.

errorCases.scenario: Entry text is longer than 500 characters.
errorCases.detection: The entry measures the length of text on creation.
errorCases.userImpact: The parser must shorten or split the entry, or it is not stored.

errorCases.scenario: A tagged name does not match the entry text.
errorCases.detection: The entry compares each entity's text with its own text between start and end, including an end beyond the text's length.
errorCases.userImpact: A wrongly positioned tag cannot reach the index.

errorCases.scenario: A time is not ISO 8601 or has no UTC offset.
errorCases.detection: The time check parses the value with the standard library and tests that the result has an offset.
errorCases.response: Failure with invalid_input naming the field.
errorCases.userImpact: Times from different machines stay comparable.

errorCases.scenario: An entry's status and retirement fields disagree: retired without a retirement time, or active with a retirement time or a replacement.
errorCases.detection: The creation check compares status with retired_at and replaced_by.
errorCases.response: Failure with invalid_input naming retired_at or replaced_by.
errorCases.userImpact: A retired entry always carries the time that purging needs.

errorCases.scenario: A retired entry is retired again, or retire is given an invalid time, the entry's own identifier or a blank replacement.
errorCases.detection: retire reads the status and checks both arguments before changing anything.
errorCases.response: Failure with invalid_input naming status, retired_at or replaced_by; the entry is unchanged.
errorCases.userImpact: A recorded retirement cannot be silently overwritten.

errorCases.scenario: Code assigns a field of an entry directly.
errorCases.detection: The frozen dataclass rejects the assignment.
errorCases.userImpact: The mistake shows up in tests of the assigning module.

errorCases.scenario: A failure is created with a blank message or an unknown kind.
errorCases.detection: The failure checks its arguments itself, without the shared checks.
errorCases.response: ValueError or TypeError, since the mistake is in the code raising it.
errorCases.userImpact: The mistake shows up in tests of the raising module.

errorCases.scenario: A package imports something its table entry does not allow, is not in the table, or modules import each other in a loop.
errorCases.detection: The import test reads every source file's imports statically and searches the module import graph for a cycle.
errorCases.response: The test fails naming the modules.
errorCases.userImpact: The developer fixes the dependency before it is merged.

edgeCases.input: An entry with no named entities.
Entry text containing non-Latin characters or emoji before a tagged name.
edgeCases.expected: Positions and length count Python string positions, so the tag matches.

edgeCases.input: The same name tagged twice at two places in one entry.
An entry read back already retired, with a retirement time and no replacement.
A retirement time earlier than the source's time.
edgeCases.expected: Accepted; the definitions do not compare times from different clocks.

edgeCases.input: An active copy of a retired entry made by code.
edgeCases.expected: Created; refusing it is the store's duty.

edgeCases.input: A rule with leading or trailing spaces, a negation and a condition.
edgeCases.expected: Text is kept exactly as given.

edgeCases.input: A source or checkpoint at position zero.

edgeCases.expected: Accepted as an offset of zero.

edgeCases.input: Two entries with equal fields, then one is retired.
edgeCases.expected: They compare equal before and unequal after.

alternativesConsidered.name: Frozen dataclasses with a retire method
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Standard-library frozen dataclasses that check themselves with the shared checks; only retire changes an entry.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Each definition is a frozen dataclass that runs the shared checks when created. Entry has one method, retire, which takes the retirement time and an optional replacement, checks them, and then sets status, retired_at and replaced_by on the same object, bypassing the freeze for those three fields only. Entries compare by value and are not hashable, since they can change.
pros: A stored entry read back compares field for field
cons: Retire must bypass the freeze deliberately
Code can still build an active copy of a retired entry, which the store refuses

alternativesConsidered.name: Private fields with read-only properties
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Entry as an ordinary class with private fields, read-only properties and a retire method; other definitions as frozen dataclasses.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Entry stores private attributes and exposes each through a property, with retire changing the private status, retirement time and replacement. Equality and representation are written by hand.
pros: No bypass of a freeze is needed
cons: Much hand-written code for properties and equality
Differs in style from every other definition
Private attributes can still be changed by code that chooses to
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: More code for no stronger guarantee.

alternativesConsidered.name: Mutable dataclass
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Entry as an ordinary mutable dataclass with a retire method.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Entry is a plain dataclass checked on creation, with retire setting status, retirement time and replacement. Nothing prevents other assignments.
cons: Any field can be assigned after the checks
A retired entry can be reactivated by assignment
Does not hold the rule that only retirement changes an entry
